idiom_name: none - the type system adds no layout control; TypedArray/DataView (or Buffer on Node) for packed small records
alternative: Use TypedArray/DataView over an ArrayBuffer (or Node's Buffer) for packed small records and keep object shapes monomorphic; TypeScript's types describe structure, not storage, so hand-rolled union encodings only lose the engine's optimizations.
implementation_notes: TypeScript compiles to JavaScript, so the runtime story is JavaScript's: object layout belongs to the engine (V8 carries a small integer inside the tagged value with no extra allocation), and the type system can only describe the shape of objects, never their storage. The practical answer for dense small values is a binary view - TypedArray/DataView, or Buffer on Node - with a manual discriminator byte and explicit offsets, plus objects that keep a single shape so the engine's inline caches stay monomorphic. Encoding payloads into a tagged object with optional members instead creates megamorphic access and unpredictable hidden classes. Treat small object optimization as an engine concern in TypeScript: what the developer actually optimizes is allocation count (reuse, pooling, avoiding per-call closures) and element packing.
pitfalls: readonly and as const are compile-time only: they document intent but make nothing smaller, immutable or allocation-free at runtime - object.freeze, not the type, is what enforces immutability (and it makes the object slower to change).

DataView/TypedArray give dense storage but hand ownership of offsets, endianness (typed arrays use platform byte order) and bounds to the programmer; unlike a class, a mis-set offset corrupts the neighbouring record silently.

Optional members and union types invite shape churn: an object that sometimes has a tag and sometimes not becomes megamorphic, so a tagging scheme that is not uniform across all instances can cost more than the allocation it avoids.
sources: MDN Web Docs, TypedArray - typed arrays are views over a binary ArrayBuffer with fixed element widths, and DataView is the explicit-endianness alternative for packed records: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/TypedArray

V8 blog, Pointer Compression in V8 - the engine already stores a small integer directly in the tagged value 'without having to allocate additional storage for it': https://v8.dev/blog/pointer-compression
